articles.title: Saudi Arabia issues first air raid alerts for Riyadh since Houthis escalated attacks
articles.summary: Residents later received the all-clear after explosions were reported in the capital.

blocks.text: Residents in Saudi Arabia's Riyadh have been given the all-clear after air raid alerts were issued and explosions were reported in the capital.
It was the first time alerts have been issued in Riyadh since the Houthis increased their attacks and declared a "maritime embargo" on the Saudis in July.

The Saudi Civil Defence sent alerts for the capital and several other regions late on Friday night and Saturday morning (local time) as the Kingdom's conflict with the Iran-backed Houthis continued to escalate.
Journalists from Reuters and AFP reported hearing explosions in the capital, but authorities have since said the danger has passed. Residents were urged to avoid gathering in crowds.
The Houthis recently seized control of the strategic port city of Mokha and Perim Island, a gateway to a key shipping route used by the Gulf state to export to Asia and Europe.
The Iran-backed group's military spokesman said the naval blockade was in retaliation for a Saudi blockade of ports and airports in Houthi-controlled north-western Yemen.
Saudi vessels have relied on that stretch of the Red Sea for oil exports since the US and Israel's war with Iran effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz.
Last week, the Houthis attacked several Saudi oil facilities with drones and missiles, causing fires which led to operations being temporarily halted.

The attacks on Saudi oil assets have directly impacted global energy markets and the price of petrol and diesel in many countries has sharply risen in recent weeks, compounding already elevated costs caused by the blockades of the Strait of Hormuz.

Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, the country's de facto ruler, has personally asked US President Donald Trump to take military action against the Houthis, two sources familiar with the matter told CBS News, the BBC's US media partner.
Trump has so far declined to involve the US military directly, offering instead to assist with intelligence and targeting support, the sources said.
A senior Trump administration official told the BBC: "We are in continuous dialogue with Saudi Arabia and the Republic of Yemen government regarding regional stability."

Earlier this week, Houthi military spokesman Yahya Sarea said the Houthis had launched drones and missiles at Saudi Arabia in retaliation for more than 450 Saudi air strikes on their territory over the past week.

The United Nations Security Council held an emergency meeting on Tuesday, during which both Yemen's government and Saudi Arabia called for more decisive action against the Houthis, who they accused of choking the Bab al-Mandab Strait as a way of applying economic pressure.
Council members agreed that freedom of navigation in the Red Sea must be maintained to prevent disruption to global supply chains.

Yemen has been devastated by a civil war that began in 2014, when the Houthis ousted the government from the capital, Sanaa. The conflict escalated in 2015, after the Saudi-led coalition of Arab states intervened in an attempt to restore the government's rule.

The fighting has reportedly left more than 150,000 people dead and triggered one of the world's worst humanitarian crises, with more than 22 million people in need of some form of aid, according to the UN.
Additional reporting by Tabby Wilson.

articles.title: The week in photos: September 12-18, 2026
articles.summary: A recap of news, sports, lifestyle, entertainment, and human interest images from the Philippines and around the globe

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — On September 14, the Bangsamoro people troop to polling precincts to elect their parliament after decades of armed struggle and historical injustices, years of painstaking negotiations with the Philippine government, and repeated electoral delays.

Election watchdogs report significant irregularities during the polls including reports of pre-shaded ballots, vote-buying, and armed individuals in voting centers. Commission on Elections Chairman George Garcia says election-related deaths rose to at least five before voting ended.

On September 16, four retired Supreme Court justices advised the impeachment court on the conviction threshold debate. Three of them took the position that the number of votes needed to remove the impeached official is not fixed at 16. Retired justice Adolfo Azcuna maintains that all 24 senators should be counted, arguing that a fixed supermajority is necessary to prevent impeachment from being misused for political purposes.

Meanwhile, former president Rodrigo Duterte appeared in person at the International Criminal Court (ICC) for the third status conference regarding his charges of crimes against humanity related to his drug war, on September 16. Duterte has been detained in The Hague since 2025, and his trial is set to begin on November 30, following the confirmation of three charges against him.

The ICC Trial Chamber III ordered the continued detention of Duterte: “The Chamber therefore finds no notable change in circumstances that warrant the release of the Accused, with or without conditions. For these reasons, the chamber hereby decides that the accused shall continue to be detained,” said the chamber’s decision.

articles.title: ‘My fear was too great’: the Pussy Riot member recruited by Russian spies to inform on fellow activists
articles.summary:
Exclusive: In her first media interview since fleeing Russia, Rita Flores describes her three years of being run by the FSB

First came the blackmail and death threats to secure cooperation,…

blocks.text: First came the blackmail and death threats to secure cooperation, then came a series of tasks, each more sinister than the last: to inform on fellow activists, to elicit personal information from protest-minded artists and – eventually – to help with a plot to kidnap and murder a Kremlin enemy.

That is how Rita Flores, a 29-year-old Russian artist, activist and former member of the Pussy Riot collective, described her recruitment and three-year handling by officers from Russia’s FSB security service, a cooperation she only broke when she fled the country last month.

Flores made details of her collaboration public in a video discussion with her lawyer, Dmitry Zakhvatov, published just days after she left Russia at the end of August. She explained she was coming clean in the hope that others in a similar situation might feel emboldened to break their ties with the FSB.

Now, in her first media interview since leaving Russia, she gave further detail on how she was recruited and run by the FSB. “For the first time in years, I feel calm. All this time I was dreaming about getting out and being able to talk about it all,” she said. The Guardian could not corroborate the details of Flores’s account, but there have been numerous cases of the FSB infiltrating opposition groups over the past few years.

blocks.caption: Rita Flores was arrested multiple times for provocative art performances as part of Pussy Riot. Photograph: courtesy Rita Flores

blocks.text: Flores, also known as Margarita Konovalova, has been associated with Pussy Riot since 2020, when she was detained after a performance near the Kremlin. She had served several short stints in jail and been subjected to surveillance and house searches on numerous occasions, which intensified after the domestic crackdown that followed the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

She was recruited after one of these police searches in February 2023, when two men stayed behind and introduced themselves as FSB officers, she said. They threatened to open a criminal case, under wartime censorship laws, over an Instagram post she had made criticising Russian killings in Ukraine. They also suggested they could arrange for her mother to be killed if she did not sign cooperation papers.

“I believed them. I believed they could do everything they said they would … My fear was too great. I was so worried for my family and also for myself,” she said. As a reward for signing, she was given a one-off cash payment of 30,000 or 40,000 roubles (£266 or £355), she said.

Her first tasks were to gather information about other opposition-minded artists in the same circles as her and report back to the FSB. The two FSB officers who recruited her became her regular handlers, she said, organising frequent meetings and largely sticking to a classic good-cop, bad-cop routine. She saw the senior officer only occasionally, a crude man in his late forties who introduced himself by a series of different names. In the end, Flores began calling him “the Jacket”, based on the shiny black suit he liked to wear. The junior officer, named Ivan, became her primary handler, and he often tried to be friendly and helpful, leaving direct threats to the Jacket.

blocks.caption: One of Flores’s handlers promised to ‘re-educate’ her until she became an ‘obedient wife’. Photograph: courtesy Rita Flores

blocks.text: “Whenever I met with Ivan and the Jacket together, Ivan was silent. The Jacket would be rude, threatening; he’d insult me as a woman. He was the devil incarnate. Then just me and Ivan would meet, and Ivan would be nice, friendly,” she recalled. “He liked to say, ‘The FSB will re-educate you, I will re-educate you, you’ll have a nice and calm life, and you’ll love Russia, have children and be an obedient wife,’” she said.
Flores said she was not supposed to tell anyone about her recruitment, but immediately told “about 20 people”, putting it down to the fact she is a “massive gossip”.

Still, she stopped short of telling the people from the art world she was meant to report on, instead claiming that she initiated conflicts with them on pretexts, designed to push them away from her and prevent them sharing sensitive information. Her two handlers kept up the psychological pressure by repeating their threats, and even the friendlier Ivan on occasion made it clear that the consequences for crossing him would be severe, she claimed.

“He tried to befriend me, but he could also be threatening. He’d calmly say, ‘they’ll kill your mother and you won’t be able to prove anything’ or ‘if you go abroad they’ll find you immediately and kill you,’ and then he would giggle, like it was all a joke. The Jacket, on the other hand, never joked. His threats were more direct.”

In time, there were fewer targets to inform on, as most of the protest-minded artists left the country. She described life in wartime Moscow as an exercise in cognitive dissonance. “Moscow is booming; restaurants, bars and clubs are opening and there are a huge number of events. But those people who understand things have empty eyes and speak empty words,” she said.
after newsletter promotion

blocks.caption: Flores claims most of the provocative, protest-minded artists have left Russia under Putin’s regime. Photograph: courtesy Rita Flores

blocks.text: Artists who stayed are careful not to produce any work that could be considered even tangentially political, she said. “People who have stayed in Russia have accepted the rules of a game. You go to a gallery and every artwork may as well come with a sign saying ‘we were forbidden from saying anything’ … there are artists who used to make strong statements, and in 2026 they are drawing flowers in a vase.”

Last May, Ivan and the Jacket first started asking her questions about Pyotr Verzilov, an activist previously linked to Pussy Riot who now lives in Ukraine and fights with the Ukrainian army against Russia. A longtime irritant to the Russian authorities, in 2018 German doctors said they believed Verzilov had been poisoned in Russia.

Flores said her handlers wanted her to get information from Verzilov, including his address in Ukraine. Then, they suggested she use her old friendship with him to arrange a meeting in Serbia. There, he would be kidnapped and killed by a waiting FSB squad, they claimed. Ivan began to pay her 50,000 roubles a month as an additional incentive to help with the Verzilov case.

Meanwhile, Flores said, she was plotting a way out. She married her partner last September, which she said was partly a way of worming out of the Serbia task, so she could claim to Ivan that her husband would never let her go on a trip to meet another man. Previously, her handlers had banned her from leaving the country, she claimed, and it was only when she contacted the lawyer, Zakhvatov, that she realised there could be a way for her to leave. The pair began scheming in secret over the details.

“They created a reality where she felt like they controlled everything, but actually it is not that hard to leave,” said Zakhvatov. In 2022, fellow Pussy Riot activists Lucy Shtein and Masha Alekhina fled house arrest in Moscow by dressing up as food delivery couriers to evade police and eventually leave Russia. Flores’s escape was less dramatic, but both Zakhvatov and Flores declined to give details, citing the need to protect methods for future cases.

blocks.caption: Having escaped Russia, Flores is now keen to help those in similar situations flee the country. Photograph: courtesy Rita Flores

blocks.text: After Flores’s escape, Zakhvatov announced a secure line for people in similar positions to contact him if they need help. Flores said she would also like to work to help others, and added that she was certain that recruitments in activist circles are a “mass phenomenon”. She said there was at least one person in her own surroundings who had informed on her before she agreed to cooperate, a fact she discovered when it turned out that the FSB had possession of a sex tape featuring her, covertly filmed by the person. Earlier this year, Poland jailed an exiled Russian activist for seven years, after it emerged he had passed information about fellow exiles to an FSB handler who had recruited him back in Russia.

Flores’s video confession at the end of last month was met with praise from some parts of the exiled Russian opposition, who commended her bravery for speaking out and explaining how the FSB operates, but also some scepticism from those who criticised her decision to cooperate for so long. Since then, Flores has been making calls to people she informed on as well as other old friends to explain herself, and said everyone had been supportive in these conversations.

“It’s not a big secret that it’s not great to work for the FSB, but fear can change a person,” said Alekhina. “It’s important that she’s now out of the country and that she said what happened to her out loud. Nobody was killed and nobody went to prison [because of her], so that is good news.”

articles.title: The ‘difficult’ Etta Rosales — and why she stands out in her one-of-a-kind generation of activists
articles.summary: Ateneo professor Melay Abao writes about the life and times of Etta Rosales, the former communist who became a lawmaker and eventually headed the Commission on Human Rights

blocks.text: Ateneo professor Melay Abao writes about the life and times of Etta Rosales, the former communist who became a lawmaker and eventually headed the Commission on Human Rights

items: Etta Rosales, a prominent activist and former chair of the Commission on Human Rights, launched her book 'Difficult: The Life and Times of Etta Rosales,' detailing her inspiring journey from political prisoner to a key political figure.
The book, written by Carmel Abao, chronicles Etta's life experiences, including her activism during the Marcos dictatorship, her leadership in human rights, and her battles with health issues.

Abao emphasized the unique sacrifices of Etta's generation of activists, highlighting their commitment to democracy without dwelling on personal losses, and noted Etta's exceptional role as a torture victim who became a lawmaker.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – She’s sharp and passionate as ever, taking time to write more than a few words on each of the book that she signed on Thursday, September 17, at the launch of Difficult: The Life and Times of Etta Rosales at the Executive House in UP Diliman, Quezon City.
She is, after all, the feisty Etta Rosales.

Former chairperson of the Commission on Human Rights (CHR) who had also served as representative of Akbayan for nine years, 87-year-old Loretta Ann “Etta” Rosales was the star of the show at the book launch organized by her family, peers, and comrades-in-arms.

Difficult tells her complex but inspiring journey from an activist to a communist cadre to political prisoner under the Marcos dictatorship — to being a key leader of a leftist political party to getting elected to Congress and to serving as head of a government body that probed human rights abuses.

Written by Akbayan’s first secretary-general and Ateneo professor Carmel “Melay” Abao, Difficult carries six chapters that chronicle Etta’s growing up years as a daughter of a military officer (a West Pointer at that); her political awakening and organizing in the communist underground after the declaration of Martial Law in 1972; marriage and motherhood; her leadership in the human rights movement and shift to mainstream politics; and her various battles with cancer, two strokes, COVID-19, pneumonia.
She would, in fact, ask her doctors: why am I still alive? “‘Malakas kasi ang puso mo (Your heart is strong),’ the doctors would tell her,” wrote Abao.
Etta herself wrote one portion of the book — the one pertaining to her second arrest and detention in 1976, when she was molested and heavily beaten.

blocks.caption: COURAGE. Etta Rosales at the launch of a book on her life, written by Carmel Abao.

blocks.text: Such a harrowing experience, and the grace and courage that enabled her to continue organizing, mobilizing, and working on the streets and within the bureaucracy, melted the heart of the late president Noynoy Aquino.
It was Aquino who appointed Etta as CHR chair shortly after he was elected president in 2010.

Quoting Butch Abad, Aquino’s former budget secretary, Abao wrote: “Etta’s greatest contribution back then was her positive influence on President PNoy… PNoy was anti-communist, Butch reveals, but this anti-communism was tempered by his interaction with Etta. Because of PNoy’s knowledge and appreciation of Etta’s life story, he gained a better understanding of why those who had similar experiences during Martial Law took on very hardline positions.”
In her remarks at the launch, Abao shared her biggest takeaway as the author: that Etta’s generation of activists is one of a kind.

“That generation needs to be recognized by my generation and those after me as the generation that risked it all — lives, personal relationships, family, careers, personal development,” Abao said. “Risked it all for the sake of our nation’s democracy. I know that every generation takes risks, but Etta’s generation of activists took risks without keeping score of what they could lose because of their activism, without dwelling on the ‘what ifs.’ What if I took that PhD instead of organizing the teachers’ union? What if I stayed above ground and never left my kids and my husband? What if I just kept silent during those Marcos years?“

blocks.caption: AUTHOR. Ateneo professor Carmel Abao after receiving the first copies of the book.

blocks.text: In the many conversations that she had with Etta for the book, Abao said that not once did the “what if” question crop up.

“Having no regrets doesn’t mean, however, that there are no costs,” Abao said. “That generation lost so many great lives that were cut short by the dictatorship. And the children of that generation suffered so much — they lost parents, endured abandonment and basically skipped their childhoods.”

But Etta “clearly stood out” from the rest — “one of a kind,” Abao added. “Because she is so many roles woven into one person – marami ang naging torture victim pero si Etta ang torture victim na naging kongresista, na naging chair pa ng Commission on Human Rights (there were many torture victims, but Etta was the torture victim who became a lawmaker and even served as chair of the Commission on Human Rights).”
Etta felt at home at the launch, which was an opportunity for old comrades to get together again.

“Each one has influenced me in my various struggles in life — above ground, underground, middle ground, and again above ground,” Etta said in her remarks. “They all had one thing in common; they kept me grounded and this helped me remain steadfast in the pursuit of my faith in humanity, its integrity and the inherent right to human dignity.”
Difficult will have a second launch on Monday, September 21 — the 54th anniversary of the declaration of Martial Law — at The Loft, Arété, Ateneo de Manila University, from 4 to 6 pm. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Cuba faces another nationwide blackout amid US fuel blockade
articles.summary: Millions were left without electricity as Cuba's aging power grid collapsed under the weight of fuel shortages, deteriorating infrastructure and US sanctions.

image.caption: A severe lack of fuel makes it difficult to supply Cuba's power plants and backup generators, which typically run on imported diesel [FILE: July 14, 2026]Image: REUTERS

blocks.text: Cuba's power grid suffered a total collapse on Friday, triggering another nationwide blackout and leaving millions without electricity as the island grapples with an ongoing US fuel blockade.
"A total disconnection of the electrical system has occurred," the Energy Ministry posted on X, as only 5% of Havana had electricity.

State-run utility UNE blamed a failure in transmission lines and unstable weather for the nationwide blackout — the 7th this year and the 12th since late 2024 — as fuel shortages and deteriorating infrastructure take their toll.
"It's one thing after another: no water, no gas for cooking, no electricity," 36-year-old Lidia Fernandez told the AFP news agency. "Honestly, I don't know how we haven't gone crazy."
Cubans say problem growing
Blackouts lasting more than 30 hours have become common in Havana, while some provinces have endured outages exceeding 60 hours.

blocks.caption: In recent weeks, blackouts have lasted more than 30 hours in the capital, while in outlying provinces, they have sometimes stretched past 60 hours [FILE: May 14, 2026]Image: Ramon Espinosa/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: The power cuts have also disrupted water supplies, cooking gas, telecommunications and transportation.
Cuba, home to more than 9 million people, is also facing a deepening economic crisis.
An independent study released this week estimated that 66% of the population now lives in poverty, up from 45% in mid-2025, citing rising food prices as a key factor.

"No one can stand these constant blackouts. There isn't enough food, there's no water, there's no electricity — you have no idea," Mercedes Rodriguez, 60, told AP. "The country is in such a sad state, and there are no words for what we're going through."
How have US sanctions impacted Cuba?
Cuba's aging power plants rely heavily on imported fuel, which has become increasingly scarce amid US restrictions imposed in January.
US President Donald Trump's administration tightened sanctions and enacted an oil embargo, choking the Caribbean country from importing fuel and replacement parts required to maintain infrastructure.
Havana blames US sanctions for worsening shortages, while Washington claims the outages reflect failures of ⁠the country's state-run economic model.
Trump has even made scarcely veiled threats to take over the island.

articles.title: Google's Gemini AI hacked 3 companies during testing
articles.summary: During a test of its cybersecurity capabilities, Google's Gemini AI model accessed the internet and hacked other companies. This is the first known instance of Google's AI systems engaging in such…

image.caption: Google's artificial intelligence, Gemini, is the latest to have hacked other companiesImage: Matteo Della Torre/NurPhoto/picture alliance

blocks.text: Google's consumer artificial intelligence (AI) model, Gemini, hacked into multiple systems by guessing login credentials during tests of its cybersecurity capabilities, the company said on Friday.
This is the latest in a series of cybersecurity breaches involving rogue AI, raising safety concerns about the technology.
The internet giant is the fourth AI developer whose programs have been found to exhibit such behavior, following OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta.
Google only made the incidents — which occurred in May and were discovered by Google in July — public after an inquiry from The Wall Street Journal.
Will AI destroy humanity?
What we know about the incident
According to the WSJ report, there were three instances in which Gemini infiltrated the computers of other companies, whose names were not disclosed.
In one case, the AI guessed passwords to access a protected system. In the other two, it found login credentials in a database.

"In a standard evaluation, the model found public information online and guessed credentials to access websites it thought were part of the test," Heather Adkins, Google's vice president of security engineering, told the AFP news agency in a statement.

"In all three of these instances, the model stopped," Adkins said. "We ensured the three entities were made aware, and we worked with our training partner on the changes they've now made to their testing processes."
What is AI's biggest risk: Speed or autonomy?
Autonomous AI agents pose risks

Similar incidents have been reported earlier by Meta, Anthropic, and OpenAI. These incidents have raised questions about the necessary safeguards as AI agents become more autonomous and gain access to the internet and computer systems.
AI model developed by OpenAI, the creator of ChatGPT, escaped from a secure environment during a test in July and infiltrated the computers of another AI company, HuggingFace, unexpectedly.
This prompted rival Anthropic to review its own test runs, during which additional incidents came to light.
Meta subsequently admitted that its AI had hacked into another company's computers due to a system misconfiguration at a testing partner.
This month, Dario Amodei, the CEO of Anthropic, called for a slowdown in AI development.
In a blog post, he expressed concern that a swarm of autonomous software systems, or AI agents, could take over the entire internet within six to 12 months, causing billions of dollars in damage.

articles.title: After SALEX tree-cutting, critics see worse traffic, health, heritage loss
articles.summary: Transportation advocates lay out potential risks posed by proposed expressways, including the controversial SALEX

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – Groups criticized proposals for new, elevated expressways, showing new research and a map of the expansive existing and proposed projects with a total valuation of at least P2.7 trillion.

“Why are we building and approving more elevated expressways in the Philippines when other progressive cities are tearing them down?” asked Ken Abante of the Move As One Coalition in Filipino during their online press conference, also joined by the Stop SALEX Movement and other advocates, on Wednesday, September 16.

While the minimum valuation of the projects is at P2.7 trillion, the number rises to P3.4 trillion if bridge projects are included. The number is based on declarations made by project proponents, so the final values may still vary upon confirmation of “appropriate government institutions and third parties.”

The groups also discovered that P1.6 trillion of the P2.7 trillion covers unsolicited projects and involves “little to no” competitive bidding processes. Unsolicited projects are project proposals “made by a private proponent.”

These groups likewise called attention to the proposed Southern Access Link Expressway (SALEX) project and its potential risks to affected communities and the environment, calling for an end to its construction.

They warned that the 40.62-kilometer expressway not only worsens traffic and affects its nearby surroundings, but also endangers and damages historical heritage sites, as it passes through major cultural and national structures.

The project forms part of a broader network of expressways planned to provide access to several major roads and transport routes. It includes access to the proposed New Manila International Airport in Bulacan.

Prior to the conference, the group, along with experts in architecture and urban mobility, also convened at the Stop SALEX Movement forum at the Ramon Magsaysay Center on September 12, raising similar concerns about traffic, health and the environment, and heritage.
Sustainable mobility advocates said that adding more expressways fails to solve traffic due to the phenomenon of “induced demand.”

“When you have more and wider roads, you get more driving,” explained sustainable mobility advocate Robert Siy Jr. during the Stop SALEX Movement forum. “People take more trips and before long, you have worse traffic.”

Beyond traffic, Siy also pointed to potential health risks, especially to those living near such expressways. Potential risks include “constant noise and vibrations” due to SALEX construction and operations.
Multiple studies have linked prolonged exposure to noise-induced stress to various health risks, including higher blood pressure, greater risk for diabetes, and neuroinflammation.

blocks.caption: ROBERT SIY JR. The sustainable mobility advocate urges the audience to write to local and national officials regarding projects such as SALEX. Photo by Lance Bustos

blocks.text: In addition, paved roads could bring about extreme heat days due to the “urban heat island effect,” according to the group’s research.

The urban heat island effect is a phenomenon where the removal of vegetation and trees, and their replacement with impervious surfaces such as concrete and asphalt results in “significantly hotter” conditions in urban areas.
Such impervious surfaces also contribute to urban flooding, as the loss of vegetation and trees can result in partially submerged or completely impassable roads, leading to reduced accessibility.
In May 2026, 617 trees were marked for removal in Manila to make way for the SALEX project, prompting public backlash and uproar among environmental groups and experts.

Heritage also became a point of discussion. Their research said that proposed and developing road projects should “account for their cultural costs so that heritage is not sacrificed for car-centric infrastructure.”A heritage group, Members of Manileños for Heritage, has mapped out 50 cultural and historical sites that could be affected by the SALEX project. This includes Paco Park, Malate Church, the Elpidio Quirino Monument, and the Jose P. Laurel Foundation Building, among many other landmarks.

blocks.caption: COVERED. A visualization of Padre Faura St. if SALEX is built.Image by CARe-Centric Ph/Facebook

blocks.text: Architect and heritage advocate Dominic Galicia pointed out that the SALEX project could become obstructions to heritage sites and affect their surroundings by decreasing visibility.

“As we walk on Padre Faura with this giant expressway overheads cast a permanent shadow over what used to be trees, what used to be sun touching the surfaces of these heritage structures… You deprive the people of the natural experience of living and walking in a city,” Galicia said.
He also pointed out that it’s “a matter of livability” as to why these heritage structures should remain visible.

“We understand who we are by the place we occupy… If you wipe out the experience of being in these places, there is nothing to experience and there is less to remember until we will no longer know who we are,” Galicia said.
The movement has also coordinated with members of the academe, particularly with Adamson University.

On June 30, the Adamson University community called for the protection of green spaces and heritage sites, with students and administrators protesting against SALEX as it will pass through the campus on San Marcelino St. in Manila. The university is considered a historical site by the National Historical Commission of the Philippines. – Lance Ariel Bustos/Rappler

Lance Ariel Bustos is a campus journalist from Santa Rosa City, Laguna, studying Political Science and Philippine Media Studies at De La Salle University Manila. An Aries Rufo Journalism Fellow for 2026, he is an editor-at-large of The LaSallian.

articles.title: Thousands protest closure of the Kennedy Center amid fears Trump is set to demolish the institution
articles.summary:
Demonstrators gathered outside the building in Washington, after the president was spotted holding a placard that read: ‘Kennedy Center DEMOLIS ...’

On Friday evening thousands of protesters…

blocks.text: On Friday evening thousands of protesters gathered outside the Kennedy Center in view of the marble facade that remained concealed by scaffolding and tarpaulins, to protest Donald Trump’s plans for the facility and express alarm that he might make good on his threat to tear down the institution.

Crowding streets in the Foggy Bottom area of Washington and locking down traffic as they walked, many carried signs, as they joined in the “Hands Around the Kennedy Center” protest. Some wore costumes and booed when the president was mentioned during the program.

Chris Raleigh, co-founder of Hands Off the Arts, which set up the gathering, said in an interview that he hoped the event would show that people are willing to fight to halt Trump’s plans for the building.

blocks.caption: Thousands of demonstrators gather outside the Kennedy Center on Friday. Photograph: Zoraida Diaz/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock

blocks.text: One of the most iconic buildings on the Potomac River waterfront, the Kennedy Center has been a focus of Trump’s remake of Washington since 2025, when he began installing favorites on to its governing board. Late last year, he had his name placed on the center. A judge ruled that Trump’s name was illegally added and ordered it removed.

The Kennedy Center board, which is aligned with the president, voted Tuesday to close the center indefinitely for repairs hours after US District Judge Christopher Cooper blocked their plans to return Trump’s name to the building. On Thursday, the judge ordered the Kennedy Center to provide 30 days’ notice before making any major physical changes to the building, including demolishing it.

The protests on Friday came after a photo of Trump examining a depiction of the Kennedy Center apparently being demolished sparked widespread attention. In the image captured by AFP photographer Brendan Smialowski on Wednesday, the president was seen through the windows of Air Force One holding a placard with visible text in red declaring: “Kennedy Center DEMOLIS...”
The rest of the word was obscured by the plane’s window frame.

blocks.caption: Donald Trump is seen aboard Air Force One checking a Kennedy Center printout. Photograph: Brendan Smialowski/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: Raleigh said he, like others, is concerned Trump could tear down the building without notifying the court. “Look at the East Wing,” he said. “We got up one morning and there was a giant hole there.”

Among the demonstrators were people in inflatable animal costumes and a man in a golden Trump mask with a crown and a sign that said: “Restore my name in gold you sycophants.” Another man wore a blue hat that said: “Make America intelligent again.”

Baby Trump balloons danced in the air against the setting sun. Protesters beat drums, chanted “hands off!” and waved signs including: “Keep your tiny hands off our Kennedy Center”; “You’re no Jack Kennedy”; “Donny you are no JFK!”; “Kennedy Center 4 ever”; “Our center not DJT’s”; “Hands off the arts”; and “Wicked starring DJT”.

blocks.caption: Drag Queen Tara Hoot holds up signs as she rallies against the closing of the Kennedy Center. Photograph: José Luis Magaña/AP

blocks.text: Friday’s event followed a tumultuous week in federal courts in Washington in which filings and counter-filings flooded the courts as the administration continued its push for the president’s vanity projects. The administration has made substantive steps to begin work on a number of projects, despite the fact they are still being litigated. Such projects include Trump’s triumphal arch and the administration’s takeover of East Potomac Golf Links and the US Institute of Peace.
Speaking from the Oval Office, Trump said he was willing to save the center, which he said was losing money. He did not address a question about demolishing it.

“We have a lot of people working very hard on it to save it,” he said. “I can save it easily, but why should we be doing that and then raise money for the rest of our lives to keep it afloat? Because that’s what you have to do, if we get no recognition. I think the Trump administration should be recognized as having saved the Kennedy Center.”

articles.title: Gemini hacked 3 companies in first known breakout by Google’s AI
articles.summary: The hacks, which occurred in May during a cybersecurity test, were conducted by Irregular, an independent company that conducts cybersecurity evaluations

blocks.text: Google’s Gemini model accessed the internet and hacked other companies during a test of its cybersecurity capabilities, the first known example of the company’s AI systems autonomously committing such an act.
The hacks occurred in May during a cybersecurity test conducted by Irregular, an independent company that conducts cybersecurity evaluations.

During a standard testing evaluation, Gemini found public information online and guessed credentials to access three websites it thought were within the scope of its test, Heather Adkins, Google’s vice president of security engineering, said in a statement.

“We ensured the three entities were made aware, and we worked with our training partner on the changes they’ve now made to their testing processes,” Adkins said. “These events highlight the importance of training powerful AI models to act responsibly.”

An Irregular spokesperson said the incident involved the same issue that affected other AI labs and that all relevant labs were notified in late July. “All known issues on our end were remedied and resolved weeks ago,” the spokesperson said.

Similar incidents linked to Irregular were disclosed by Meta, Anthropic and OpenAI. Meta said in August the incident did not involve a sandbox escape or sophisticated cyberattack, while Irregular said it was working on best practices for securely conducting AI cybersecurity evaluations.
The incidents have raised questions about the safeguards needed as AI agents gain greater autonomy and access to the internet and computer systems.

In one of the cases, the Gemini model guessed passwords until it gained access to a protected system. In the other two cases, the model found credentials in a public repository that allowed it to then access protected systems, according to the Wall Street Journal, which first reported the news on Friday.
Adkins said that in all three instances, the model ceased its hacking. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Wanderlust wins: Singapore Airlines says travel demand still taking off
articles.summary: 'We are very positive about the market, and we do see people are still very interested to travel,' Singapore Airlines general manager Liewei Tai tells Rappler

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – Even as higher fuel costs put pressure on airfares, Filipinos don’t seem ready to put their travel plans on hold.

Singapore Airlines (SIA) continues to see strong appetite for travel from the Philippines, although passengers are becoming more conscious of how much they are getting for what they spend, according to Liwei Tai, the airline’s general manager for the Philippines.
“I think we see that people are still interested to travel. Perhaps there is a greater awareness now about the value that they get when they travel,” Tai told Rappler on Thursday, September 17.
Tai’s focus on value is unsurprising, as airlines are also grappling with higher fuel costs that can eventually translate into more expensive tickets.

SIA Group’s net fuel cost surged more than 78% year-on-year to S$2.25 billion in the April-to-June quarter, following the escalation of the conflict in the Middle East. But, it turns out, that hasn’t kept travelers from coming in droves: Singapore Airlines and its low-cost subsidiary Scoot carried a record 10.9 million passengers during the quarter, 6.3% more than a year earlier.

The trend continued into August. The two airlines carried 3.7 million passengers worldwide, up 3.6% year-on-year. And while those figures cover the global network and can’t be attributed specifically to Philippine routes, Singapore Airlines still has a bullish view of the local market.

“For the Philippines, we already added an additional flight out of Manila last year. We are very positive about the market, and we do see people are still very interested to travel,” Tai told Rappler. “We will continue to be here together with Scoot, also our subsidiary airline. We will want to continue to grow in the Philippines over time.”
The airline increased its Manila-Singapore service from four to five flights a day in May 2025, while Scoot launched flights between Singapore and Iloilo in April that year.

Philippine aviation data tell a similar broader story about Filipinos’ willingness to fly. Scheduled international airlines carried 15.27 million passengers to and from the Philippines in the first half of 2026, according to Civil Aeronautics Board data. That was already equivalent to about 52% of the 29.12 million international passengers recorded for the whole of 2025.
For travelers, then, pricier fuel may be changing the calculation more than cancelling the trip altogether.
Tai said SIA is seeing demand across a wide mix of travelers, from solo and business passengers to groups of friends and families, including several generations traveling together.

“We see now different kinds of traveler profiles. Of course, we have families, family with young children, especially in the Philippines, where family is so important, even multi generational travel. But even then, we have friends who are traveling together, even solo travelers, business travelers,” she said.

Beyond fares and flight options, Tai said SIA is also seeing improvements in the travel experience at Ninoy Aquino International Airport (NAIA), now under private management by New NAIA Infra Corp. (NNIC). NAIA may still have a long runway before it can rival Singapore’s Changi Airport, but Tai said the changes are already becoming noticeable to passengers. (READ: Two years and billions later, has NAIA finally leveled up?)
“We do see the improvements as well,” she said, pointing to shorter queues and quicker baggage retrieval. “I think there is very close coordination between different parties to make that possible.”

SIA is also currently holding its latest Time to Fly Virtual Travel Fair with Mastercard, offering discounts of as much as 37% on flights to destinations including Singapore, Sydney, London, Paris, Los Angeles, Manchester, and Madrid. – Rappler.com

articles.title: NMC says China Coast Guard placed civilian lives at risk when it rammed BFAR vessel
articles.summary: The National Maritime Council on Saturday said the ramming done by the China Coast Guard on a vessel of the Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources in the West Philippine Sea placed civilian lives…

blocks.text: Published September 19, 2026 10:35am

The National Maritime Council (NMC) on Saturday said the ramming done by the China Coast Guard (CCG) on a vessel of the Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources (BFAR) in the West Philippine Sea (WPS) placed civilian lives at risk.

"The National Maritime Council (NMC) expresses its serious concern on the 18 September 2026 incident involving the Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources (BFAR) vessel, BRP Datu Magat Salamat (MMOV 3015), and China Coast Guard (CCG) vessel, CCG 21585, as reported by the National Task Force for the West Philippine Sea (NTF-WPS)," the NMC said in a statement.

"The NMC is particularly concerned that the illegal, coercive, aggressive, and dangerous actions of the CCG vessel placed the civilian crew of the BFAR vessel at unnecessary risk while carrying out a legitimate livelihood-support mission," it added.

"The NMC underscores that safety of life at sea must always come first. All vessels operating in the area are expected to exercise maximum restraint, professional seamanship, and due regard for applicable international maritime safety rules," the statement read.

"The NMC supports the coordinated response by the NTF-WPS, particularly the Philippine Coast Guard, BFAR and other concerned member agencies, in ensuring the safety of the vessel and its crew and the continued delivery of assistance to Filipino fisherfolk," it added.

Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) spokesperson for WPS Rear Admiral Jay Tarriela said CCG vessel 21585 rammed the BRP Datu Magat Salamat while the Philippine vessel was carrying out its maritime patrol and fuel subsidy mission for Filipino fishermen on Friday.
Tarriela said that at 11:04 a.m., the Chinese vessel reportedly cut across the stern of the BFAR vessel at a distance of only about 10 meters.
At 11:13 a.m., while the BRP Datu Magat Salamat was maintaining its course, the Chinese vessel repeated the maneuver and made contact with the BFAR vessel, striking it.

The Philippine vessel sustained damage on its starboard side including the bent, broken, and detached; deformed metal stanchions and support structures deformed; and displaced deck fixtures and equipment displaced, with debris scattered across the deck.
After the collision, CCG-21585 conducted another dangerous maneuver, passing dead astern at a distance of only about five meters, according to Tarriela.
The incident occurred around 6.36 nautical miles north-northwest of Abad Santos Shoal and about 54 nautical miles from Palawan's coast, within the Philippines' exclusive economic zone (EEZ).

"The Philippines will continue to exercise its sovereign rights and jurisdiction in its exclusive economic zone consistent with UNCLOS and the 2016 Arbitral Award, while pursuing a peaceful and rules-based approach to maritime differences. Our seas are part of our national identity and patrimony," the NMC said.

"We will continue to support our fisherfolk and government personnel who serve the country at sea, and we will remain steadfast in upholding our lawful rights and national interests in our maritime domain with courage, unity and respect for the rule of law," it added.

The Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) meanwhile said there was “no justification” for the CCG's aggressive actions that resulted in a minor collision with a Philippine civilian vessel in WPS on Friday.

"The Philippines calls on China to respect Philippine sovereign rights within its exclusive economic zone in accordance with UNCLOS as affirmed by the 2016 Arbitral Award, exercise restraint and avoid actions that could further escalate tensions in the region," the DFA said.
GMA News Online reached out to the Chinese Embassy for comment on Friday but it has yet to issue a statement. —KG, GMA News

articles.title: No justification for China Coast Guard to ram BFAR vessel — DFA
articles.summary: The Department of Foreign Affairs said there was no justification for a China Coast Guard vessel to ram a Philippine civilian vessel conducting a humanitarian mission in the West Philippine Sea.

blocks.text: September 19, 2026 | 10:18am

MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Foreign Affairs said there was no justification for a China Coast Guard vessel to ram a Philippine civilian vessel conducting a humanitarian mission in the West Philippine Sea.
The DFA condemned the incident involving the Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources’ BRP Datu Magat Salamat, which sustained damage after being struck by China Coast Guard vessel CCG-21585.

“There is no justification for the CCG vessel to undertake aggressive actions against a Philippine civilian law enforcement vessel, and cause damage to the ship and endanger the safety of the civilian crew,” the DFA said in a statement posted on Facebook on Friday night, September 18.
"The Philippines emphasizes that the BFAR vessel was merely conducting routine and lawful humanitarian activities to support Filipino fisherfolk in the West Philippine Sea," it added.
BFAR vessel damaged

The Philippine Coast Guard said the incident happened at around 11 a.m., about 54 nautical miles off Palawan, while the BFAR vessel was carrying out a mission to assist Filipino fishermen in the Kalayaan Island Group.
The vessel was delivering fuel subsidies and food packs to Filipino fisherfolk following weeks of monsoon rains, according to the PCG.
PCG spokesman for the West Philippine Sea Rear Admiral Jay Tarriela said the Chinese vessel intentionally rammed the BFAR ship.
“To call this unprofessional or bullying would be an understatement. What we are seeing here is pure evil,” Tarriela wrote on Facebook with a video of the incident.
The impact damaged the BRP Datu Magat Salamat’s main railings on the starboard side, metal stanchions and support structures, as well as deck fixtures and equipment. No injuries were reported.
Tarriela said the CCG vessel later made another dangerous maneuver, passing behind the BFAR vessel at a distance of about five meters.
The BRP Datu Magat Salamat was refloated Thursday after running aground at Hasa-Hasa Shoal while approaching Filipino fishing boats to distribute fuel.
Tarriela said the vessel would be brought to Coron Port for an assessment of its seaworthiness.
DFA cites international law
The DFA said the Philippine vessel was conducting routine and lawful humanitarian activities to support Filipino fisherfolk.
“The CCG vessel's illegal, coercive, aggressive and dangerous acts are inconsistent with China's obligations under international law,” it said.

The department noted that the Chinese vessel’s actions were inconsistent with China’s obligations under international law, citing the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, the 2016 Arbitral Award, the 1972 International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea and the 1974 Safety of Life at Sea Convention.

“The Philippines calls on China to respect Philippine sovereign rights within its exclusive economic zone in accordance with UNCLOS as affirmed by the 2016 Arbitral Award, exercise restraint and avoid actions that could further escalate tensions in the region,” it added.
Beijing blames Philippine vessel
The Chinese embassy in the Philippines disputed the Philippine account of the incident in a statement posted on Facebook.

Jiang Lue, a spokesperson for the China Coast Guard, said the Chinese vessel Sanzhou'ao was conducting what Beijing described as rights-protection and law-enforcement operations near Xianbin Jiao in China's Nansha Qundao on September 18.

According to the statement, the Philippine vessel No. 3015 ignored repeated warnings from the Chinese side, deliberately altered course and suddenly accelerated before cutting across the bow of the China Coast Guard vessel, resulting in a collision.

“The Philippine side's actions seriously violate international law and the basic norms of international relations and threaten the safety of China Coast Guard vessels and personnel,” the statement said.
The Chinese Coast Guard said its vessel operated “in a professional and standardized manner, reasonably and lawfully” and placed full responsibility for the collision on the Philippine side.
It also demanded that the Philippines stop what it described as “infringing and provocative acts,” warning that consequences arising from such actions would be borne by the Philippine side.

"The China Coast Guard will continue to carry out rights-protection and law-enforcement operations in waters under China's jurisdiction to safeguard national territorial sovereignty and maritime rights and interests," it added.

articles.title: Can Quezon City rediscover its history?
articles.summary: Rapid development has made Quezon City a commercial hub, but it hopes to bring its rich history back in public view

blocks.text: Quezon City’s cultural identity has long suffered from a split personality: one side driven by commercial expansion and the other buried beneath its historical roots.
So in defining its cultural heritage, Quezon City Mayor Joy Belmonte hopes to address one question: “How do you find the real soul of a city built from a blueprint?”

Long before stepping into public office, Belmonte studied archaeology at University College of London in the 1990s alongside the late Filipino archaeologist Dr. Victor Paz. That training taught her to read a city like an excavation site.
”People aren’t really aware [of the city’s cultural heritage] because they don’t really identify with Quezon City, and maybe that’s the problem — that it’s a created city,” said Belmonte.
University of the Philippines’ faculty archaeologist Ligaya Lacsinan, who has been with the institution since 2021, noted that lack of awareness stems directly from how the city was created.

Belmonte shared that during focus group discussions to brand the city, they discovered that for some, QC meant being “jologs” or someone who has a tacky taste or outdated fashion; some just see it as a city “named after Quezon;” while some just associate it with “shopping malls.”
Residents’ perceptions of the city also differ depending on the communities they identify with, Belmonte said.

The mayor pointed out that the city’s microgeographies have been linked to various meanings or activities, like the internet satires on New York, Cubao; vintage hunting at Cubao Expo; Sunday jogging at UP Diliman; or the nightlife in Tomas Morato.
“This disconnect manifests in the way our citizens speak in microgeographies,” Belmonte said.
Established in 1939, Quezon City is only 87 years old, younger as a city than places like Manila and Cebu. But a relatively recent development does not equate to lack of history.
Belmonte admitted that Quezon City was once negatively associated with informal settlements.
“[During the] ’70s and ’80s, Quezon City was called ‘the squatter capital of the Philippines,’” she said.
Yet, the original vision for the city, which has 142 barangays and 6 districts, was different.

Former Philippine president Manuel L. Quezon envisioned a “City of Man,” a green, human-centered capital designed for ordinary working-class families — a contrast to Manila’s imperial Burnham Plan, a 1900s urban design created by American architect Daniel Burnham.

blocks.caption: The UP Balara Filters Park located next to the UP Diliman campus in Diliman, Quezon City.

blocks.text: The QC plan, also known as the Frost Plan, remains visible today in the city’s quadrangles, sprawling public parks, and pioneer socialized Projects from 1-8.
Belmonte pointed to the city’s planned public spaces and residential communities as evidence of that vision.
“Kaya dun sa original plan ni Robert Frost, meron tayong Quezon Memorial Circle (The Quezon Memorial Circle is in the original plan of Robert Frost),” she said.
Today, the city’s green spaces remain among its most visible features, including three parks: the La Mesa Eco Park, Ninoy Aquino Parks and Wildlife, and UP Diliman Balara Filters Park.
Beyond its parks and urban landscape, Quezon City also traces its hidden heritage in archaeological and historical sites scattered across its neighborhoods.
Belmonte noted how Quezon City’s roots lie directly within the Novaliches sector.
”Our oldest prehistoric remains are from Novaliches, the La Mesa Watershed,” Belmonte said.
The city extended a direct pledge to the UP School of Archaeology to fund new local excavations and construct a dedicated city museum.
“Baka gusto niyo maghukay sa La Mesa watershed, habang mayor pa ako, gawin natin (While I’m still the mayor, you might want to do the excavations at the La Mesa watershed),” Belmonte said.
“We would love to show in a museum that we have prehistoric culture in Quezon City.”

blocks.caption: Ang Sigaw ng Pugad Lawin by Napoleon Abueva located in Project 8, Bahay Toro in Quezon City. Photo courtesy of the Quezon City Government

blocks.text: Heritage, though, is not limited to archaeological artifacts. Historical memory can also be preserved in places associated with figures from the Philippine Revolution.
In Balintawak and Banlat, for instance, Melchora “Tandang Sora” Aquino is remembered for nursing wounded Katipuneros during the revolution.
Belmonte recounted the time how her administration worked hard to reclaim Tandang Sora’s birthplace from urban decay.
By 2025, the site launched the Museum of Women’s history to what we now know as the Tandang Sora Shrine.
“Time naman ng dad ko (former Quezon City mayor and representative Sonny Belmonte), he set up a shrine at nilipat namin ang labi ni Tandang Sora doon sa Tandang Sora Shrine,” Belmonte recalled.
(During my father’s time, former Quezon City mayor and representative Sonny Belmonte, he set up a shrine and transferred the remains of Tandang Sora to the Tandang Sora Shrine.)

The city also commemorated late president Quezon’s pre-World War II humanitarian initiative — saving over 1,000 Jewish refugees fleeing the Holocaust — when it inaugurated a park in the Quezon Memorial Circle in 2018.

In celebrating Quezon’s legacy, the city government moved Quezon’s actual residence from Gilmore Street to the Memorial Circle with the help of Jerry Acuza, who started the Las Casas Filipinas de Acuzar known for moving old houses.
The move was a loan, a meticulous preservation effort, Belmonte shared.
“On loan po sa akin ang lahat ng mga damit, gamit ng Quezon family (All the clothes and artifacts of the Quezon family are on loan to me),” she said.

blocks.caption: The Quezon City Memorial Shrine in honor of late Philippine president Manuel L. Quezon. Photo courtesy of the Quezon City Government

blocks.text: Other historical sites within the city’s neighborhoods include San Pedro Bautista Church in Frisco and the Pugad Lawin area in Bahay Toro.

The Ang Sigaw ng Pugad Lawin monument, created by National Artist Napoleon Abueva in 1988, also serves as a physical reminder of Andres Bonifacio and the Katipuneros’ “punitin ang sedula (tear up the cedulas)” rebellion on August 23, 1896.
Belmonte highlighted how historical consensus reframes Quezon City as a true cradle of the Philippine Revolution, citing historian Professor Xiao Chua.
“You have to call yourself the birthplace of the nation,” Belmonte recalled Chua saying.

blocks.caption: Mayor Joy Belmonte talks about Quezon City’s cultural heritage in a lecture at UP Diliman.

blocks.text: Belmonte encouraged professionals, students, and artists to participate in shaping the city’s historical narrative through initiatives such as Bayanihan QC, a volunteer program to help the city’s projects and activities.
The Heritage Trail passports initiative also encourages residents to visit historical sites across Quezon City.
“Every time you go to one of these sites, you stamp your passport and you get something free kapag natapos mo lahat (when you complete it),” Belmonte shared.
For residents, understanding Quezon City’s heritage may ultimately come down to seeing familiar places differently.

UP Anthropology graduate Nadia noted that the fast pace of urban life often blinds residents to what lies right beneath their feet: “We in QC are too busy living our lives, we kinda miss these invisible things that are actually obvious.” – Rappler.com
Jade Tan is a Rappler intern studying AB Journalism at University of Santo Tomas.

articles.title: More than 35 woman come forward in case against fake 49ers player accused of fraud
articles.summary:
The FBI says Daejon Love and his alleged accomplice, Taylor Chan, defrauded women they met on dating apps out of $1.3m

At least 35 additional women have come forward with fraud allegations…

blocks.text: At least 35 additional women have come forward with fraud allegations against Daejon Love, the man accused last month of masquerading as a San Francisco 49ers player and wealthy investor, the FBI announced on Friday. Federal authorities had previously said Love conned more than two dozen women, many of whom he met on dating apps, out of $1.3m.
Love, 35, and alleged accomplice Taylor Chan, 18, who posed as his financial adviser, were arrested in August and have been charged with wire fraud.
A public defender for Love and Chan’s attorney did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Love allegedly used a combination of AI-assisted fake identities, fabricated investment accounts and staged video calls with Chan to gain the confidence of women in California, Idaho, Washington and Oregon, according to federal authorities. To some women, he claimed to be a former NFL player, to others he claimed he said he was on reserve or injured.
Love convinced several women who believed they were dating him that if they sent him money for investments, it would yield high returns.
The plot allegedly began around February 2022 up through the time of the pair’s arrest in August, according to prosecutors. Federal authorities have not publicly revealed how Love and Chan met.
In court documents, prosecutors described Love as nomadic, saying little is known about his family ties and that he has no known legitimate source of employment.
Since his arrest, texts and videos where Love flaunted a seemingly lavish lifestyle and 49ers paraphernalia have gone viral on social media, much to the amusement of some online users.
At a Friday news conference, Portland FBI special agent Douglas Olson criticized any jokes levied at the women ensnared by Love’s scheme.
“Victim blaming is unjust and it’s harmful and it overlooks the calculated, highly manipulative lengths these individuals went to deceive and exploit others,” Olson said.

“Victims were encouraged to take out personal loans and make life altering financial decisions based on the belief they were building a future with someone they cared about. Once the money was taken, the victims were cut off, left without answers, without funds, and often without closure. Many lost not only their savings, but their sense of security and confidence,” he said.
Olson urged any other potential victims to contact law enforcement.

articles.title: Did the NCAA really partner with a gambling site?
articles.summary: The NCAA denies entering into a partnership with PlayTime Entertainment, an online gambling platform, yet the brand appeared multiple times during the league's opening-day broadcast

blocks.text: STAR. Titing Manalili (13) in action for the Letran Knights in the NCAA Season 102 men's basketball tournament.
NCAA Philippines Facebook page
The NCAA denies entering into a partnership with PlayTime Entertainment, an online gambling platform, yet the brand appeared multiple times during the league's opening-day broadcast

items: The NCAA clarified that there is no partnership with PlayTime Entertainment, despite initial promotions suggesting otherwise.
PlayTime Entertainment's branding was featured during NCAA broadcasts, leading to confusion and criticism, especially regarding gambling's influence on a student audience.
An investigation is underway to determine how PlayTime Entertainment was promoted, as the NCAA management committee had previously rejected their sponsorship proposal.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
There’s no existing partnership between the NCAA and online gambling platform PlayTime Entertainment.
The NCAA made this clarification after it drew flak following PlayTime Entertainment’s supposed entry as the league’s “official entertainment partner” and “season presenter” for Season 102.

“For the avoidance of doubt, no agreement has been executed and no signing of any kind has taken place between the NCAA and PlayTime Entertainment,” the NCAA management committee said in a statement released on Wednesday, September 16.

“Accordingly, any statement or representation suggesting that PlayTime Entertainment has entered into such a partnership with the NCAA is inaccurate and does not reflect any agreement authorized or entered into by the NCAA.”
If so, then what is all the fuss about?

PlayTime Entertainment materials were visibly featured in the opening-day broadcast on Sunday, September 13, its logo shown multiple times throughout the double-header, which saw St. Benilde stun defending champion San Beda, and Letran beat Perpetual.

NCAA broadcaster Cignal TV also aired a speech by PlayTime Entertainment spokesperson Adela Mae Marshall twice: first before the St. Benilde-San Beda clash, when she delivered her statement live, and again as a replay at halftime of the Letran-Perpetual duel.

“Today marks an important milestone for Playtime Entertainment as we enter a new space for sports and become part of one of the country’s most prestigious sports leagues. We’re truly honored to be a part of the NCAA Season 102 as we believe that sports is a powerful space that brings people together,” said Marshall.
“This partnership is very significant to us because we believe that the power of sports is to create connections and shared experiences.”
But that Letran-Perpetual match ended up being the last time PlayTime Entertainment promotions appeared in the NCAA as the ensuing games no longer featured them.
PlayTime Entertainment has also removed most of its social media posts relating to the NCAA.
“The NCAA remains committed to ensuring that all official partnerships and engagements relating to the league are communicated accurately and through the appropriate channels,” the league said.
So what happened?
According to an NCAA source, league officials were left surprised to see PlayTime Entertainment promoted during the broadcast since the management committee rejected its entry.

blocks.caption: Did the NCAA really partner with a gambling site?

blocks.text: While not all of the 10 member schools opposed PlayTime Entertainment’s proposed sponsorship, the NCAA still turned it down because the management committee, the source said, prefers a unanimous vote on such matters.
As it turned out, a league-commissioned agency negotiated with PlayTime Entertainment and went directly to Cignal TV, which was unaware that the NCAA already rejected the proposal.
“Cignal, knowing that this outfit is commissioned by the NCAA, it entertained them,” the source said. “They were not aware.”
When asked if the agency went behind the NCAA’s back, the source believes it did.
“It looks like that. We were not aware that something like this was happening,” the source said.
The NCAA has launched an investigation and has reached out to both the agency and PlayTime Entertainment.
“What could happen is that they could be terminated,” the source said about the agency. “Because bottom line, we have no idea why that happened.”

It did not take long for the promotion of a gambling site in a varsity league to raise eyebrows, given that collegiate leagues like the NCAA caters to students, many of whom are below the legal gambling age. In the Philippines, only individuals who are at least 21 years old are legally permitted to gamble.

But it’s not the first time a sports event drew criticism over gambling matters as the Philippine National Volleyball Federation (PNVF) faced scrutiny over the appearance of 1xBet, an online gambling brand not registered in the Philippines, as a sponsor of the 2025 FIVB Volleyball Men’s World Championship, which the country hosted.
The issue reached the Senate, with Senator Erwin Tulfo strongly blasting the PNVF not only for 1xBet’s involvement but also for high ticket prices of the global showdown.

blocks.caption: Tulfo, Hontiveros blast FIVB world volleyball ticket prices, gambling ads

blocks.text: Former PNVF president Ramon “Tats” Suzara clarified that logos of 1xBet, which he said is an official partner of the FIVB, appeared only on global broadcast feeds and were excluded from the local broadcast. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Trump signs broad Russia sanctions bill
articles.summary: The bill signed by US President Donald Trump targets officials, banks, and a fleet of shadow tankers that transport Russian energy.

image.caption: The bill targets the so-called "shadow fleet" that moves Russian energy [FILE: March 2026]Image: Miguel Medina/AFP

blocks.text: US President Donald Trump signed into law a package of new sanctions against Russia named after the late Senator Lindsey Graham, the White House said on Friday.
Earlier, the bill passed Congress with large bipartisan majorities: 86-11 in the Senate and 262-159 in the House.
The comprehensive sanctions package is intended to punish and pressure Moscow for its ongoing war against Ukraine.
In addition to the sanctions on Russia, the law establishes a framework to maintain sanctions on Iran until 2031.
What sanctions does the bill include?
The bill targets Russian officials and key sectors of the Russian economy, including banks, and a fleet of shadow tankers that transport Russian energy.
It also instructs Trump to impose tariffs of up to 100% on the top five importers of Russian oil or natural gas. However, some countries are exempt.
The US president can also impose sanctions on the five countries that do the most to help Russia circumvent energy sanctions.
These measures could further strain US trade relations with China and India, both of which buy significant amounts of Russian oil.
How India has become Russia's trade lifeline
What are the reactions?
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy thanked Trump for signing the bill, as well as all the senators and members of the House of Representatives who supported it.
"When Lindsey Graham was here in Ukraine, he would always talk about how important it was not to ease pressure on Russia, to strengthen sanctions and seek a path to peace," he wrote on X.
Graham, who played a leading role in advancing the bill, was a staunch supporter of Ukraine. The senator had just returned from Ukraine when he unexpectedly passed away in July.

"The best way to honor Lindsey's memory will be to implement the provisions of this law fully and swiftly. And the best reward for everyone helping us put pressure on Russia to end its war will be peace," Zelenskyy added.
Before Trump signed the bill, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov warned that additional US sanctions would hinder efforts to achieve a peaceful resolution in Ukraine.

articles.title: Possible EV link in June Aster fire prompts ferry bans, safety review
articles.summary: Shipping firms impose restrictions as the June Aster fire investigation continues.

blocks.text: September 19, 2026 | 9:09am

This handout photo taken on September 11, 2026 and released by the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) shows a burnt vehicle and the burnt frames of motorbikes in the cargo hull of the M/V June Aster off the shores of Coron town, Palawan province.
Philippine Coast Guard / Handout via AFP

MANILA, Philippines — The possibility that an electric vehicle was involved in the explosion aboard the fire-hit MV June Aster has prompted shipping companies and government agencies to evaluate safety protocols for transporting EVs and hybrid vehicles by sea.

Since last week, Philippine Coast Guard investigators have been trying to determine the cause of the incident following survivors' accounts that they heard a loud explosion from the ship's cargo deck before the fire broke out.
The Coast Guard said it is looking into several possibilities, including a terrorist attack or an explosion involving the EV aboard the vessel.
The MV June Aster was carrying one EV, five motorcycles, a forklift, a pickup truck and other cargo when it was engulfed in flames on September 9.
Authorities stressed that they have not determined the cause of the fire, as the investigation remains ongoing.
Developing safety guidelines
This week, at least two shipping companies announced restrictions on EVs and hybrid vehicles aboard their vessels.
In a memorandum dated September 16, Montenegro Shipping Lines Inc. announced that hybrid and electric vehicles would no longer be allowed aboard its passenger and cargo vessels across all routes.

"The measure is being implemented as a preventive safety precaution to minimize the risk of fire, explosion, thermal runaway, and other potential hazards associated with electric and hybrid batteries during vessel operation," the memorandum read.
Another shipping company, Island Water, also released a memorandum on September 17 restricting EVs and hybrid vehicles aboard its passenger vessels.

"In consideration of marine safety standards and risk management regarding alternative powertrain technologies and high-capacity battery systems, this measure is enacted to ensure the utmost safety and protection of all passengers, crew, and cargo during transit," it said.
The Department of Energy (DOE), meanwhile, said Thursday, September 17, that it recognizes the safety concerns raised over the transport of EVs by sea.
The agency said it is coordinating with the Maritime Industry Authority (MARINA) and other concerned agencies to develop broader safety guidelines for transporting EVs aboard vessels.
